title: A continuation can defer every inherited blocker defect and still count as delivery; the defect ledger has no severity
summary: Split from continuation-findings-anchor-first (its absorbed continuation-remediation-first-contract half). The repair-first directive for inherited red predicates landed with that item. Still open: cycle 1573 deferred 19 of 19 inherited defects, both parent blockers among them, and the defect-ledger gate counted it as delivery (wave 3 went 0/3). gradeClaim knows no severity (core/defectledger/reconcile.go), and the Entry schema has none (core/defectledger/schema.go).
root_cause: The defect ledger grades a DEFERRED disposition the same for a blocker and for a nit, so a continuation can carry its parent's blockers forward without a repair.
fix: Console design task (core/defectledger is protected). (a) Give each ledger entry a severity taken from the audit finding that minted it. (b) Refuse a DEFERRED disposition of a blocker-class inherited defect, or refuse the continuation at mint. (c) Optional, overlaps posthoc-diff-anchor-no-op-cycle: derive the build-report Changes table from `git diff --cached --name-status` instead of the builder's text (1572-M1, 1574-M1).
acceptance: A defect-ledger entry carries a severity from the audit finding that minted it (red test first).
A continuation that disposes a blocker-class inherited defect as DEFERRED fails the defect-ledger gate, or is refused at mint; a non-blocker DEFERRED with a reason still passes (twin test).
go vet, the touched package suites with -race, and the defect-ledger package note updated.
connects_to: continuation-findings-anchor-first (the parent; its repair-first half landed)
posthoc-diff-anchor-no-op-cycle (the derived Changes table overlaps it)
notes: Filed by the console build of continuation-findings-anchor-first on 2026-10-20, so that the absorbed acceptance is not lost when the parent is consumed.
